Messages.Body:
Hi Methuselahs,
I have observed a great deal of comment about thoughts betrayed
lately, mostly pointing out it is a broken card. I am not at all sure
that I agree with this.
For one thing, only the superior version of TB is really useful,
as the inferior version would have you spending two blood before combat
to do one damage to your opponent at the end of each round, hardly the
optimum card for my combat decks.
Thus it follows that for TB to be really dangerous, you need
vampires with superior Dominate, not something all that common in combat
decks. You are likely to find it with Tremere, so I will address them
seperately.
In building a competitive deck, it is necessary to do at least
one thing reliably and consistently. In order to acomplish this, you tend
to put in lots of certain types of cards, ala stealth, etc. In the case
of a combat deck, you need to reliably get into combat with the minion of
your choice, and then reliably and consistently pummell said minion. Now,
this is fairly easy to accomplish with decks based on Celerity (and
Potence), or with Protean and Fortitude, at least the pummelling part.
Both of these deck types do require something else to enter combat,
typically Bums Rush / Haven uncovered, (or Intercept for
Toreador/Tremere), thus not leaving a whole lot of room for Dominate
skill cards. Additionally, you really don't have the extra turns
necessary to "build" superior Dominate onto your combat Vampires if you
are playing in a competitive environment.
So for this card to be a real game breaker, it is reasonably safe
to say you need to have Dominate as a disipline of your vampires when you
get them into play, especially superior Dominate. This basically leaves
you with Malkavians (non-combat), Ventrue (non-combat), Tremere, and a
couple of Brujah and Toreador from DS. In fairness, I haven't yet tried
to make a Brujah / Toreador Guns and Celerity deck with only dominate
vamps, however I have used it extensively with Tremere. The results have
been good, but not game breaking.
I have found the two blood cost of the card to be pretty well
balancing, even with six taste of vitae in my deck. Admitedly, my weekly
games are very difficult, our group has been playing aggressive NL games
for more than a year, and we have well designed and competitive decks.
Still, I haven't even been able to alter anyones deck building strategy
by including TB in my Tremere deck. It simply makes them as good as other
combat decks.
I am open to discussing other potential flaws with TB, but as yet
I haven't found them to be a problem in our games.
Algustas

As far as Obedience goes...

Tom is under the impression that the 'at the last moment' errata to the
'before combat' phrase of this combat card is sufficient to allow other
'before combat' phrased cards (action modifiers and reactions) to have
precedence.

Why this is so is still elusive. Treat the 'at the last moment before
combat' as 'at the first moment of combat' and everything works as Tom
claims it should (and then the combat card will be played *during* combat -
and added bonus for those preferring rules over exceptions).

>combat and watch helplessly as your foe deals out enough agg damage to

Thoughts Betrayed -
change superior to: Opponent cannot play any cards /during the first round/
of combat.

Why try to base the deck entirely around TB combos? I've found that Tremere
decks (or any deck for that matter) that depend on specific, multi-card
combos as the primary weapon are destined to have trouble. This is simply
due to the probability inherent in any card-based game.

your vampires have dominate, a few skill cards and some thoughts betrayed
will make them _much_ better in combat. When you can already hold your own,
getting a card which can effectively paralyze your opponent for an entire
combat equals torpor.

I appologize in advance for the continuation of a Magic comparison.

Above, someone compared TB to the Magic card Spirit Link as an example of
how a cards originally intended use could be twisted to the forces of
evil. The major difference (and the most important one) between TB and
Spirit Link is that Spirit Link can be dealt with. TB cannot. If someone
finds some clever use for Spirit Link, you can Counter Spell it,
Disenchant it, Tranquility it, Enchantment Alter it, Terror the critter,
STP the critter, Fireball the critter, ect., ect.,ect. Once someone
Thoughts Betrayed's you, it's all over.

If you run into a TB combat deck (Tremere, Giovanni, Euro-Brujah), and
they play a TB on you, you will be torporized or burned. No ifs, ands or
buts. You can't defend yourself in any way, and permanent combat won't
help, because if they are a combat deck (and they are), they will be able
to counter act your one manuver from your gun, counter act your piddiling
gun damage (using Acrobatics, Immortal Grapple, Blood Fury, or Blood
Stealing strikes, for instance), and you will just stand around while they
either Blur+Torn Signpost+Burning Wrath you, or they steal your blood,
press, Blood Fury, press, and Walk of Flame you off this immortal coil.

There is only one reliable counter to the offensive use of TB, and that is
the Elisium, which is unique, fragile, and can be stolen (by vamps with
DOM I might add...), so that is hardly a sure thing.

As a defensive card, it is acceptable, as guns will work fairly well
against a Malkavian using TB (minimal combat ability and no damage
prevention), and the Ventrue were already immune to combat, so it has
little bearing on them. It is in the Offensive where it is entirely out
of control.

(See. There wasn't that much about MTG...)

Add my vote to the house rule listing for TB as "Niether Minion may play
cards until the end of combat" (If only we could convince the local
Tremere player of that...)

-Peter D Bakija

Uh, yeah. Whatever.

S:CE, which is a much more powerful ability than it should be for its cost
(usually nothing) is avoided by Immortal Grapple, Hidden Lurker, Fast
Reaction, and yes, Thoughts Betrayed.

Thoughts Betrayed, on the other hand, which is generally regarded as a
fine card for defensive purposes (thought to be it's original intent), is
way to powerful for what it costs when used in an offensive fashion in a
Tremere or Pot/Dom deck (Giovanni or Euro-Brujah). Basically, an
attacking vampire gets to pay 2 blood to vaporise his victim. The only
vaguely reliable defenses to TB are The Elisium and Mariel, both of which
are _very_ fragile.

For your convinience, I repeat my discounting of all stated defenses
against TB. Please refute at your leisure:

Thoughts Betrayed, it is pretty much agreed, is a perfectly reasonable
defensive card, but when used in an offensive combat deck (Tremere,
Giovani, Euro-Brujah) it becomes an insanely powerful card. The counters
mentioned above only work to varying degrees against the offensive TB
deck. If one assumes that a deck is built as either Bruise and Bleed deck
(I go to bleed you for 5 using Govern the Unaligned, or you block me and I
kill you...) or a Rush combat deck backed up with Thoughts Betrayed, it is
a good probability that the deck will have A) Adaquate manuvers and
presses, B) A consistent way to kill you, and C) A way to avoid damage or
ignore weapons. Given all of these assumptions (which are in no way
unreasonable for a well designed combat deck), the various counters for TB
quickly fall apart:

-Permanent combat options (guns, flak vests, ect): Against a competent
combat deck, these will be all but usless in the face of TB. Guns can
easily be nullified by a single manuver card (or another gun) and a card
that either restricts the use of equipment (Immortal Grapple, Blood Fury,
Drawing out the Beast), prevents damage (any FOR card, Dodge+multi
strikes, Theft of Vitae), or does away with the equipment (Shattering Blow
or Fast Hands). The Giovani are probably the least equiped for this (they
only have Immortal Grapple and Shattering Blow), but the Tremere and the
Euro-Brujah (the Brujah with DOM ) are very good at nulifying permanent
combat, and then burning you. The Flak Vest/Resplendant Protector option
does little in this case, as how is 1 point of damage reduction going to
save you from a Blur+Torn Signpost+Burning Wrath combo?

-Locations (Elisium and the Cops): Locations are very delicate, as they
can be Arsoned or Rampaged. The Elisium can also be voted out, and as
locations are unique, a clever TB combat deck could pack their own
Elisium, just to contest yours at an opportune moment. Also, locations
can be stolen, either by a vote or by Kine Dominance, which ironically can
be used by the same folks as TB...

-Mariel, Lady Thunder: She is just asking for it. She is always the
first vampire to burn when she is played, as some combat deck will either
rush her and slay her (especially as she can't play TB if the acting
player plays it first), or she will be Malkavian Dementia'd, Ozmo will be
rushed and torporized, and then Mariel will go and diablerize him ("Hey!
We the Nosferatu are outraged!"). Talk about 2 birds with one stone.

-The Master Element (Frenzy, Brujah Frenzy, Rotschreck): These are a wild
card, as they may or may not help. Brujah Frenzy is a good one, as it
makes Constantine Vinti go and pulp your preys vamp instead (or, it
encourages Constantine to manuver to long range and flip your preys vamp
the bird, as they both laugh at you). At least it will save you for one
turn. Frenzy (I don't have one, and I don't really remember it well), I
think will only save you from the Tremere, as the Brujah and Giovani want
to get to close range and beat you with their Hands anyway. I can't
really see a TB/Guns deck be worth making. Rotschreck is such a
interperitation nightmare that hardly anyone uses it, as no one can agree
on who it is supposed to screw with (I say the vamp about to Recieve
aggro, as why would Basilia suddenly be undeathly afraid of her hands, but
that's just me).

-Basilia: She has the same problem as permanent combat. All she can do
in the face of TB is stand around and try to poke you, while the TB vamp
is manuvering and killing her from range, dodging and add'l striking, or
preventing all her damage. Now you are out a 10 point vamp. Sad.

It seems that the best defense against Thoughts Betrayed in an offensive
mode is to have Mariel and Elisium out at the same time, have a hand full
of Brujah Frenzies and Deflections (to avoid the Bruise/Bleed strategy),
and a whole lot of itty bitty Caitif to intercept the stealth free Bum's
Rushes (so you don't feel bad when they are martyred). If that is not the
basis for a deck design, I don't know what is.

-Peter D Bakija

As the Corrupter mentioned, the greatest power of TB is that you can have
any good combat deck and then throw in some TB to make it infinitely
better. Most combat decks are pretty card combo intensive. The Tremere
need alot of cards (get in combat, strike/damage avoidance, press,
manuver, strike, ect...), the Brujah need alot of cards (get in combat,
manuver, strike, aditional strike, damage avoidance, press...). Ventrue
gun deck needs alot of cards (get into combat, a gun, manuver, damage
prevention, ammo, press, ect...). Basically any combat deck is card
intensive, as opposed to a vote deck (which basically requires a one card
combo) and S+B (which requires a 2 card combo). Considering how all
combat decks are card intensive anyway, how is it debilitating to add ONE
extra card to the combo to make your combat power 700%(+/-) more
effective?

You do not need to build a deck around TB to make it effective. The
Tremere can make fairly effective decks already, either a Bleed/Burn or an
Intercept/Kill deck. They also have plenty of vamps with DOM. Just chuck
a few TB in the deck, and every once and a while, the fairly effective
Tremere deck will become ungodly powerful with only limited extra cost.
Many people use the archtypical Brujah Rush deck. There is no reason not
to modify it a bit by putting in Constantine or Donal or a few Dom masters
and some TB. How does the deck suffer? Perhaps every once and a while
you will get a vampire sucko deal and have to discard your TB's 3 or 4
times, but then you are playing the old (and very effective already)
Brujah rush deck. If you DO get a good combo, your deck becomes much more
effective, again at limited cost.

People are currently debating the usefulness of the Tremere, so that is
not needed to be done here, but I have seen the Tremere be very effective,
and TB just adds to that effectiveness, in a somewhat unbalancing way.

All in all, one could build an all TB-Combat deck and make it very
effective, or one could just add some TB abilities to an already effective
combat deck and make it even more effective, again, at a cost that is
outweighed by the benefits.

As for the "Clan Hoser" side line, it is very ineffective to put a bunch
of clan hoser cards in your deck just in case one of them shows up, unless
you know what clans are being played. If you know what clans are being
played, and you put clan hosers in just to screw them, that is rather
unsporting (atleast around here). Most of the clan hosers are not all
that powerful, so taking up the card space just for gamble is just not
worth it. For instance, Brujah Frenzy stops one Brujah action, so at
best, it is going to keep you alive for 1 turn. Nosferatu Putrescence is
a fairly weak card to nix a fairly weak clan. Letter from Vienna is
pretty harsh, but is duplicated by the far more versatile Consenguenious
Condemnation. All those cards are hardly worth the deck space considering
how much of the time they will be useless. The sole exception to this is
Malkavian Dementia, as there is almost always some Malkavian around (as
they are such a no-brainer, usually) and it is powerful enough to justify
its space useage even if it might be useless. With Malk Dementia, you can
ususally kill off two vamps with that one card, if it is planned well
(take control of one Malk, sneak over and diablerize another one, Blood
Hunt the first.). That is far more worth the deck space in ones deck
propper than Brujah Frenzy, which does little more than, say, keep one of
your vamps alive for one turn (or one action...).

-Peter D Bakija
